findings.title: deleteCache success does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status on screen
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop; unlike the disconnect mutation right below it (which invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars in onSettled), it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query. The query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt is configured with refetchOnWindowFocus: false, so in any usage of SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper where the optional onChanged/onSuccess callback is not provided, the dropdown will keep showing "Cache Status / Last updated: <timestamp>" and the "Delete cached data" action for cache rows that were just deleted, until a full page reload. Add an onSettled invalidation of utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars to deleteCacheMutation so the cache status disappears after deletion.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hardcoded to en-US formatting, ignoring the user's locale
findings.body: The 'cache_last_updated' timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }). Every user, regardless of their configured locale, will see US-style dates (e.g. 7/15/25, 3:04 PM), which is confusing for locales that use DD/MM/YYYY or 24-hour times. Use the user's locale (e.g. navigator.language or the i18n locale from useLocale) instead of the hardcoded "en-US" string.

findings.title: Handler throws a generic Error, surfacing as HTTP 500 instead of 404/403
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user, deleteCacheHandler does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In tRPC a plain Error is reported to the client as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500), which is wrong for a not-found/authorization failure and will also pollute server error monitoring. The codebase convention is to throw a TRPCError with an explicit code, e.g. `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: ... })` or FORBIDDEN, so clients get the correct status code.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache mutation or the cache-status repository method
findings.body: This PR adds a data-deletion endpoint (viewer.calendars.deleteCache) plus CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, but no automated tests. The important behavior to lock down is the authorization check: a user must not be able to delete CalendarCache rows for a credentialId owned by another user (the handler only checks prisma.credential.findFirst({ id, userId })), and the not-found path should raise the expected error. A regression here would silently let one user wipe another user's availability cache. Add handler tests covering the owner, non-owner, and missing-credential cases.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId adds an extra DB write on the webhook hot path for a value nothing reads
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now ends with SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}), which updates (and bumps @updatedAt on) every SelectedCalendar row for the credential. fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache runs on every Google Calendar webhook notification and cache repopulation, so this adds a write query per webhook event. Per the PR's own notes, SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is not displayed or consumed anywhere in the frontend — the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt — so this write buys nothing and, worse, makes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt meaningless as a staleness signal for any future consumer. Consider removing it until there is an actual reader.

findings.title: sed -i '' syntax is macOS-only and fails on GNU/Linux
findings.body: The script updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with `sed -i '' -E "s|...|..." "$ENV_FILE"`. The `-i ''` form (separate empty-string argument for the backup suffix) is BSD/macOS-only; on GNU sed (Linux dev machines, CI containers) the empty string is parsed as a filename and the command fails with "sed: can't read : No such file or directory", so the .env file is never updated. Use a portable form (e.g. `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"`) or detect the platform.

findings.title: ENV_FILE="../.env" resolves relative to the caller's working directory and can write outside the repo
findings.body: The script hardcodes ENV_FILE="../.env", which is only correct when the script is invoked from inside the scripts/ directory. A developer running `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root (the natural way to run it) will have ../.env resolve to the parent directory of the checkout; the script then either edits an unrelated .env there or, per its own fallback, creates a brand-new .env outside the repository containing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Resolve the path relative to the script's own location instead (e.g. ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/.env").
